title: Flood
summary: Turn around, don't drown. Get to higher ground and stay out of the water.

sources.title: NWS: Turn Around Don't Drown (driving through floodwater)

items.text: Know your risk. Check FEMA's Flood Map Service Center.
items.note: Flooding does not follow the lines on a map.

items.text: Sign up for your community warning system. Emergency Alert System and NOAA Weather Radio also send alerts.
Flood insurance: homeowner's policies do not cover flooding, and a new policy can take up to 30 days to start.
Make a household plan that includes pets. Practice evacuation routes and shelter plans.
Keep non-perishable food, cleaning supplies and water for several days.
Keep papers in a waterproof container, with password-protected digital copies.
Move valuables to higher levels, and clear drains and gutters.
Under a flood warning, **find safe shelter right away**. Evacuate if told to.
**Never walk, swim or drive through floodwater.** Turn around, don't drown.
items.note: 6 inches of fast-moving water can knock an adult over. 12 inches can carry away most cars. 2 feet can carry away SUVs and trucks.

items.text: Never drive around barricades. The pavement underneath may have collapsed.
Stay off bridges over fast-moving water. They can wash away without warning.
Trapped in a vehicle in fast-moving water: stay inside. If water rises inside, get onto the roof.
Trapped in a building: go to the highest level. **Do not climb into a closed attic.**
items.note: Go onto the roof only if you must, and signal for help once there.

items.text: For a medical emergency, call 911. Otherwise contact your healthcare provider and wait for instructions.
Monitor the Emergency Alert System, NOAA Weather Radio or local alerts.
Return home only when officials say it is safe. Avoid driving except in emergencies.
Avoid wading in floodwater.
items.note: It may be contaminated or hide debris, and downed or underground power lines can electrify it.

items.text: Do not touch wet electrical equipment or anything while standing in water. Turn off electricity if it is safe to.
Wear heavy work gloves, protective clothing and boots. Use a mask when cleaning mold or debris.
items.note: People with asthma, other lung conditions or weak immune systems should avoid buildings with mold or indoor water leaks. Children should not help.

items.text: Watch for snakes and other animals in your home.
Run generators and gasoline-powered equipment outdoors only, away from windows.
Do not drink tap water until it is confirmed safe. Boil or treat it if unsure.
